episode.tagline: Good things happen to us when we give them the chance to do so. The more we put ourselves out there, the more we are likely to get lucky.
episode.about: In this episode, Amit shares his fascination with the phrase, the Surface Area of Serendipity. And together, Ajay and Amit explore the delicate balance between excellence and exposure that is required to be both good and successful.

items.content: Amit's opening thank-you: there are 'eighty-four trillion videos on YouTube' and 'eight billion people on this earth, constantly…
Ajay on famous panellists: once they go on a conference stage, 'you end up having to say world peace.' Such star-studded events, he…
Ajay on youngsters who want to join an open-source project for three months to put GitHub on their résumé: 'And I just want to kick them…
Ajay on the 'content-free hustlers who are just trying to go out and schmooze and actually know nothing.'
Ajay's zero-transmission-loss world: Jimi Hendrix steps out of his bathroom, plays for one person and runs back in, 'because then you're…
After Ajay says Amit knows when he's speaking with dead intent: 'You are always dead serious with me, as I'm sure. And I'm never dead…
Ajay credits Amit with saying 'every time another person succeeds a little part of me dies.' Amit: 'I didn't say that. I quoted a…
Amit roasts his co-host: watch world cinema even 'if you watch one film every three years like Ajay Shah here.' Later: 'Increase your…
Amit calls the young crew on camera, 'Run, run. Run faster... Stop running,' then credits them for everything good about the show: 'All…
Amit's pitch for Magic Fruit: watch it so that 'thirty years later, forty years later, perhaps ninety years later, if you're thirty and…
Ajay explains moving back to India in 1993 with the lyric: 'Would you exchange a walk on part in a war for a lead role in a cage?'
'Youth is wasted on the young,' says Ajay. 'Indeed, and wisdom is wasted on the old,' replies Amit. At the end Amit returns to it: Magic…
Amit's shorthand for India's scarcity-driven, goal-directed culture: 'IIT bharti ho, IIM karo, Citibank mein Vice President bano.'
Ajay's examples of lifelong devotion: Linus Torvalds writing the Linux kernel unpaid, Ken Thompson, Jimi Hendrix, Jimmy Page and Tracy…
Richard Stallman's line 'a good programmer will never starve,' which Ajay uses to argue that a day job can coexist with a serious craft.
Ajay accepts the role of luck with a song lyric: 'I don't know why fortune smiles on some and lets the rest go free.'
Amit explains his introvert reluctance with Sartre: 'hell is other people.'
'There are no strangers, there are just friends you don't have yet,' attributed to Tom Robbins's Even Cowgirls Get the Blues.
Atticus Finch and Boo Radley from To Kill a Mockingbird: most people turn out to be nice once you get to know them.
'Superconnector,' the term Ajay introduced to Amit before the recording. Amit says Ajay is one, linking people across disciplines.
Carpe diem, 'seize the day,' as Amit's summary of Dead Poets Society and its famous last scene.
